title: Isolation of leukemia-derived extracellular vesicles from mouse spleen using ultracentrifugation
author: Gargiulo, Morande, et al.
materials: Timing: 4 h sEV isolation and purification

steps.title: Identify diseased mouse
steps.instruction: Select a leukemic Eμ‑TCL1 mouse (≥50 weeks old) that has ≥70 % CD5⁺CD19⁺ cells in peripheral blood (flow cytometry).

steps.title: Prepare instruments and harvest spleen
steps.instruction: Sterilize surgical tools, set up a cold dissecting surface, euthanize the mouse, excise the spleen and keep it on ice.

steps.title: Prefill gentleMACS tube
steps.instruction: Fill one gentleMACS tube per spleen with 5 mL cold PBS (Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺‑free) on ice (use up to 10 mL if the spleen is very large).

steps.title: Prepare 17 % OptiPrep cushion
steps.instruction: Make 17 % OptiPrep solution, filter all buffers (including OptiPrep) through a 0.22 µm filter, and store at 4 °C (stable ≤6 months).

steps.title: Transfer cleared plasma
steps.instruction: Move the cleared spleen plasma (minimum 7 mL, maximum 8.5 mL) into a 9 mL thick‑wall ultracentrifuge tube (16 × 76 mm) and draw a vertical line on the outer side of the tube to mark the pellet position.

steps.title: First ultracentrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 110 000 × g for 70 min at 4 °C (acceleration = 0, brake = 9) using an MLA‑55 fixed‑angle rotor; proceed immediately after the run stops.

steps.title: Discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Invert the tube, place it upside‑down on absorbent paper, and let all liquid be absorbed; keep the drawn line pointing upward to protect the pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend first pellet
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL cold PBS (Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺‑free) to the pellet (or PBS containing 200 nmol L⁻¹ BioTracker MemBright 488 dye if fluorescent labeling is required).

substeps.instruction: Pipette up‑and‑down with a 1 mL syringe fitted sequentially with a 200 µL tip then a 1 mL tip.
Optional: incubate 30–40 min at 4 °C to aid dispersion; if dye is used, keep on ice ≥15 min.
Avoid direct tip‑pellet contact, prevent bubbles, and verify complete dispersion.

steps.title: Dilute with PBS
steps.instruction: Add 3 mL cold PBS (Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺‑free) to bring the volume to 4 mL.

steps.title: Prepare cushion tube
steps.instruction: Prefill a 5 mL thin‑wall polyallomer ultracentrifuge tube (13 × 51 mm) with 1 mL of the 17 % OptiPrep cushion.

steps.title: Layer sample onto cushion
steps.instruction: Gently layer the 4 mL resuspended sEV on top of the OptiPrep cushion using a low‑speed pipetting tool (e.g., pipette boy set to release = 0 or a 1000 µL manual pipette with minimal plunger force).

steps.title: Second ultracentrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 100 000 × g for 70 min at 4 °C (acceleration = 0, brake = 9) using an MLS‑50 swinging‑bucket rotor; proceed immediately after stop.

steps.title: Collect interphase
steps.instruction: After the run, a pale interphase ring containing sEV appears below half the tube volume.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate 3 mL of liquid above the interphase without disturbing the ring.
Collect up to 1 mL of the interphase (sEV) by pipetting from the pale ring, staying above the bottom pellet of membrane debris.

steps.title: Second wash ultracentrifugation
steps.instruction: Transfer the 1 mL interphase to a fresh thick‑wall ultracentrifuge tube, add 7.5 mL cold PBS, and draw the vertical line outward as before.

steps.title: Third ultracentrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 110 000 × g for 70 min at 4 °C (acceleration = 0, brake = 9) using the MLA‑55 rotor; proceed immediately after stop.

steps.title: Discard supernatant again
steps.instruction: Decant the supernatant, keeping the drawn line pointing upward to avoid resuspending the pellet.

steps.title: Final pellet resuspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend the sEV pellet in 500 µL (maximum 1 mL) cold PBS (Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺‑free).

substeps.instruction: Use a 1 mL syringe with a yellow (p200) tip followed by a blue (p1000) tip; pipette until the pellet is fully dispersed.
Avoid direct tip‑pellet contact and bubble formation; confirm no visible aggregates remain.

steps.title: Filter sEV preparation
steps.instruction: Pass the suspension through a 0.45 µm filter (4 mm) using a 1 mL syringe.

substeps.instruction: If the sEV will be used immediately, filter a second time through a 0.22 µm filter (4 mm).
If the filter clogs, replace it promptly; do not force filtration to avoid loss of material.

steps.title: Save aliquot for protein assay
steps.instruction: Take a small volume (e.g., 4.5 µL) of the filtered sEV for protein quantification (Bradford assay or equivalent).

steps.title: Aliquot and store sEV
steps.instruction: Dispense 100–200 µL aliquots into Eppendorf tubes and store at –80 °C; avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles.

description: The protocol described here has been optimized to isolate small extracellular vesicles (sEV) from the spleen of the pre-clinical murine transgenic models of leukemia Eμ-TCL1. The protocol can also be applied to spleens derived from control mice (C57Bl/6) injected with TCL1 cells (adoptive transfer models; AT) and healthy control mice (HC).1.Identify the animal that has reached an adequate stage of the disease (typically a leukemic Eμ-TCL1 mouse above 50 weeks of age).2.Prepare sterile surgical instruments and surface to dissect the mouse and harvest the spleen.3.Prefill a gentleMACS tube (1 per spleen) with 5 mL (max 10 mL if the spleen is of considerable size) of cold phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) without Ca2+ and Mg2+ and keep it on ice.4.Prepare the 17% OptiPrep needed for sEV isolation using ultracentrifugation.Note: The preparation of all buffers and reagents must be completed prior to euthanizing the mouse to ensure a swift harvesting process. All solutions should be filtered with a 0.22 μm filter before use. Spleens should be maintained at low temperature following the harvest.CRITICAL: To ensure that sufficient amounts of sEV are collected for subsequent analyses, it is recommended that leukemic mice (transgenic or AT) reach at least 70% of CD5+CD19+ leukemic cells in peripheral blood (PB), measurable by flow cytometry.2
